clue.text: Well, son, perhaps the estimate is too high

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the words are only one possible version of themselves, so their letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A father reassures his son that a gloomy forecast is overstated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of WELL and SON; 'the estimate is' only sets the scene for the definition: an estimate that is too high is inflated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inflated beyond its true size, like an exaggerated figure, is puffed up.

clue.text: Badly arranged, as a train containing nothing to accommodate invalids

indicators.note: containing means the scrambled letters hold another piece inside them
badly arranged tells us the letters of the following words are put in a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A railway timetable is so badly organised that sick passengers have nowhere to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' suggests the railway, but it is only fodder; 'to accommodate invalids' defines by purpose, the plural of sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanatoria are institutions built to house and treat people recovering from long illnesses.

clue.text: Jealous playmate

definitions.meaning: the most famously jealous husband in drama, Shakespeare's Moor
read as play-mate: the husband (mate) who gives his name to a Shakespeare play

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Moor of Venice is the archetype of jealousy and is the title spouse of a tragedy.

clue.text: The small print suggests a more vulgar action

definitions.meaning: small letters as opposed to capitals
lower means coarser and case means a lawsuit, an action at law

explanation.definitionFit: Printers kept small letters in the lower tray; separately, a coarser lawsuit would be a baser legal action.

clue.text: Cow short of water

definitions.meaning: an old word for cattle, as in neatherd
a drink served without any water or mixer

explanation.definitionFit: The old word for bovine animals also describes undiluted spirits.

clue.text: Father severe with Dr Johnson for his ignorance of this word ?

definitions.text: Dr Johnson for his ignorance of this word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
stern means strict or severe

explanation.surface: A harsh parent scolds the great lexicographer for not knowing a word.
explanation.walkthrough: Dr Johnson's Dictionary defined a horse's pastern as its knee; asked why, he answered 'Ignorance, madam, pure ignorance.'
explanation.definitionFit: The part of a horse's leg between fetlock and hoof is the term the lexicographer famously got wrong.

clue.text: Bonds particularly suitable for real estate

parts.note: proper means fitting or especially appropriate
ties are bonds or links

explanation.surface: Investment advice: certain bonds suit a property portfolio well.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in answer order, so the second piece of the clue comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses and land owned are holdings, a synonym for real estate.

clue.text: Noisy card games

parts.note: bangs of doors, and the winning of every trick in bridge, share one word

explanation.definitionFit: Bridge players bid grand or little ones, and doors banged hard make the same sound-word.

clue.text: Man of taste finds sound remedy for Silas's protégée

indicators.note: sound tells us to go by how the phrase is said rather than spelt

parts.note: Eppie is the girl Silas Marner adopts in George Eliot's novel, and a remedy is a cure

explanation.surface: A gourmet discovers a healthy medicine for a novel's young heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Silas Marner, the miser of George Eliot's novel, raises the orphan Eppie; 'Eppie cure' said quickly matches the word for a gourmet.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of refined taste in food and drink is a gourmet, named after Epicurus.

clue.text: Secular for the time being ?

definitions.meaning: split as non and CE: not belonging to the Church of England, so worldly
an idiom for the present occasion

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'for the nonce' means temporarily, and NON-CE splits as not Church of England, so worldly.

clue.text: Sound, expert knowledge ? Not by any means

indicators.note: sound signals that a word is to be said aloud and its spelling ignored

parts.note: know-how is practical skill or expertise

explanation.surface: A question about expertise is answered with a flat refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: The silent K of know-how disappears when spoken, leaving the dialect word for 'in no way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect adverb meaning in no way or under no circumstances.

clue.text: It makes trouble to share cut ardent love

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
to ration is to share out in fixed portions

explanation.surface: Passionate love causes trouble when it must be divided between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It makes' joins the pieces to the definition; the page's 'cut' is a misprint of 'out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship or deep devoted affection is the meaning of the noun.

clue.text: Labourers lose nothing to top craftsmen

indicators.note: lose tells us a letter drops out of the word for labourers

parts.note: toilers are people who labour hard
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Workers who lose out end up beneath the master craftsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top craftsmen' are those who work on top of a building: roofers.
explanation.definitionFit: Roofers who lay slates or tiles on a building's top are craftsmen working up high.

clue.text: Get another policy to restore confidence

definitions.meaning: take out a fresh assurance (insurance) policy
to put someone's mind at rest again

explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to put their mind at rest; split as re-assure, it means insure again.

clue.text: Giving an insincere kiss ?

parts.note: a kiss is given with the mouth, so a hollow one is support offered only with words

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means professing support or loyalty without any real commitment behind it.

clue.text: Miss Fleming's hoard, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lady's private stash of savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhoda Fleming is the heroine of George Meredith's 1865 novel of that name; the scan's 'board' is a misprint of 'hoard'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of a Victorian novel by George Meredith bears this first name.

clue.text: What 2 and 11 do

parts.note: the entries numbered 2 and 11 in the grid share a square, crossing one another

explanation.definitionFit: Lines that cross each other at a point are said to cut across one another.

clue.text: Memorable note from Zinoviev, ostensibly

definitions.meaning: as of a saint's day printed in red on old calendars, one marked out as special
the 1924 Zinoviev letter, supposedly from a Soviet (Red) leader, was a forgery

explanation.definitionFit: Saints' days were printed in red on calendars, so a special day is so called; the Zinoviev letter was a supposed communist missive.

clue.text: Private confrontation at bullfight?

parts.note: a bull and a matador meet face to face, literally head to head

explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for a private conversation between two people means literally head to head.

clue.text: He gets a direction in writing

definitions.text: He gets a direction in writing

parts.words: He gets a direction in writing
parts.note: a direction here is the name and location written on a letter, and he is its recipient

explanation.definitionFit: The person a letter is sent to is the one whose details are written on it.

clue.text: What the parricide does or wants

definitions.meaning: split as de- plus sires: a father-killer takes away his sires

explanation.definitionFit: A parricide kills his father, so he de-sires; the ordinary verb means longs for.

clue.text: Thomas's attitude is questionable

parts.note: the apostle Thomas would not believe in the resurrection until he saw the wounds, and the same word means to question

explanation.definitionFit: The apostle Thomas refused to believe without proof, hence uncertainty or scepticism.

clue.text: Fabulous supporter of the King's Arms

definitions.text: Fabulous supporter of the King's Arms

parts.words: Fabulous supporter of the King's Arms
parts.note: the royal coat of arms is held up by a lion and a one-horned mythical beast

explanation.definitionFit: The mythical one-horned horse stands as a heraldic supporter on the British royal arms.

clue.text: Ready with nothing but a shawl

parts.note: ready, or readies, is slang for cash
mere means nothing more than

explanation.surface: Someone with only spare money and a wrap to their name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' here is a noun: ready money, cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine wool from Kashmir goats, and a wrap made from it, as in a soft woollen stole.

clue.text: Gave up, like some tennis players we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us to take the word as it is spoken

parts.note: seeded players are those ranked in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: Several tennis players reportedly gave in.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield, so the past tense means surrendered.

clue.text: Coffee for the doctor — and tea

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
cha, or char, is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Ordering hot drinks for the doctor and someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine coffee named after the Yemeni port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Flying from Mecca he goes to Riga perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps implies an alternative version of the city name, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves Mecca and heads for the Latvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges RIGA; HE is taken as it is and 'goes to' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hegira was Muhammad's flight from Mecca to Medina in 622.

clue.text: Sinister birth-mark

parts.note: in heraldry a diagonal stripe to the left was supposed to mark illegitimate birth

explanation.definitionFit: A bend sinister is a heraldic band running diagonally from the top right, said to mark a bastard line.

clue.text: Tried vice as a possible form of instruction

indicators.note: a possible form of the words means their letters are put into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A guide to sin offers a sample of wickedness as a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: An order or official guidance issued by an authority.

clue.text: Too much French point in this figure of speech

parts.note: trop is French for too much
E, east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Overuse of French in a rhetorical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphor or similar non-literal use of language is a rhetorical device.

clue.text: Free the song-birds of the gramophone era

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
an age is an era

explanation.surface: Releasing the singing birds of the old record-player days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'song-birds' are caged pets; 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To discage is to let out from a cage, so to release captive birds.

clue.text: Vile river of France ?

parts.note: a tributary of the Rhône whose name also follows the phrase for harsh imprisonment, used before vile

explanation.definitionFit: Durance vile is a stock phrase for harsh imprisonment, and the Durance is a river in Provence.
